Pinwheels and Ribbons Cowl is a simple piece that allows you to knit one pinwheel and one ribbon at a time; you knit some pins straight, and then you knit some pins backwards to get ribs. To create the tight, seamless tubular shape of the cowl without joining a seam, you connect a row of pinwheels with a series of ribbons. It's all completely "natural" in every way, and a joy to knit. You can do three or four rows of ribbon for a small teepee, or a long, more streamlined "drape" (a row of pinwheels makes the fabric wide, and a row of ribbon keeps it from folding in; that's why you need fewer rows of ribbon). When I was first developing this pattern, I worked up a lot of swatches just for fun, which resulted in some really pretty pinwheel and ribbon "curtains", so there you go.
